reference_answer: Yes, scheduled raw event data exports deliver event- and session-level data daily to S3-compatible storage. They aren't self-serve or real-time and are part of the Enterprise plans, so you need to contact the team.

answer: Yes, Plausible offers scheduled raw event data exports that deliver event- and session-level data from your account to your object storage every day [1]. These exports are part of our Enterprise plans and are delivered daily to your S3-compatible object storage [2].

evidence.title: Scheduled raw event data exports
evidence.text:
The Stats API and CSV export give you aggregated data: totals, breakdowns and time series across your sites. For cases where you need the underlying event-level data, Plausible offers scheduled raw event data exports.

## What it is

A scheduled raw export delivers event- and session-level data from your Plausible account to your object storage every day.

Setup is configured with our team: we agree on the data fields and schema, the delivery destination and whether the export uses CSV, Parquet or JSON Lines (JSONL).

We can deliver to any S3-compatible object storage service, including AWS S3 and Google Cloud Storage. Once configured, exports are delivered daily with no action needed on your end.

Unlike the Stats API, which returns pre-aggregated results, raw exports give you individual event records.

This lets you run your own aggregations, apply custom attribution models, join analytics data with other business data, and meet compliance requirements that call for event-level audit trails.

Raw exports are intentionally scoped to keep Plausible fast, privacy-friendly and predictable. They are not real-time and not self-serve.

## Explore an example export

Download an example export for plausible.io covering July 2026:

- events.parquet contains the individual event records
- sessions.parquet contains the sessions those events belong to

Use these files to inspect the Parquet schema and example values before planning how you will load the data into your own systems.

If you need event-level data rather than aggregated stats, Plausible offers scheduled raw event data exports as part of our Enterprise plans. These cover advanced use cases such as data warehousing, internal analytics and compliance reporting.

Exports are delivered daily to your S3-compatible object storage. See the full guide for example Parquet files, supported formats and the policy on historical backfills.

question: I built a site for my client and the project is done. How do I hand it over to them?
reference_answer: In the site's Danger zone, use Transfer site, choose Another Plausible account and enter their email. They must accept within 48 hours, and the subscription doesn't transfer, so they need an active one of their own.
key_facts: Transfer from Danger zone by sending a request to the recipient's email
Recipient must accept within 48 hours
Subscriptions are not transferred with the site
answer:
You can transfer ownership of a site to a different user by following these steps:
1. Go to site settings for the site you want to transfer [1]
2. Click **Danger zone** in the left sidebar [1]
3. Under **Transfer site**, select **Another Plausible account** and enter the recipient's email address [1]
4. Click **Send transfer request** [1]

citations.quote: 1. Go to site settings for the site you want to transfer
2. Click **Danger zone** in the left sidebar
3. Under **Transfer site**, select **Another Plausible account** and enter the recipient's email address
4. Click **Send transfer request**

evidence.title: Transfer ownership of a site
evidence.text:
1. Go to site settings for the site you want to transfer
2. Click **Danger zone** in the left sidebar
3. Under **Transfer site**, select **Another Plausible account** and enter the recipient's email address
4. Click **Send transfer request**

The recipient will get an email notification. They need to log in (or register for a Plausible account) and accept the request within 48 hours. If they don't have an active subscription, they'll need to upgrade before accepting.

After the transfer, you keep **Guest Editor** access to the site. The new owner can change your role or remove your access at any time.

### If accepting goes over your team member limit

Everyone with access to the site, including the previous owner, moves with it and counts toward the new owner's team member limit. If that's the only limit the transfer goes over, click the arrow on **Accept** and choose **Accept without members**. The site joins your account on its own, and nobody else keeps access. To bring them along, choose **Upgrade to accept** instead.

question: i added the class plausible-event-name=Button+Click on my button and made a goal called Button+Click but it shows zero conversions
reference_answer: The goal name must match the event name exactly, including capitalisation. The `+` in the class name is replaced with a space, so the class `plausible-event-name=Button+Click` sends the event `Button Click`. A goal named `Button+Click` won't count anything, so name it `Button Click`.
key_facts: Goal name must match the event name character for character
The + in the class name becomes a space
The event name here is `Button Click`
answer: The most common mismatch comes from the `+` sign in CSS class names, where the class `plausible-event-name=Button+Click` sends the event name `Button Click` with the plus replaced by a space [1]. If you created a goal called `Button+Click` instead of `Button Click`, nothing will be counted [1].

question: how do i make sure we dont get locked out if our one admin disapears
reference_answer: Keep at least two people as team owners, each with their own Plausible account, and make sure new owners accept their invitation. An Admin, Editor or Guest isn't a backup owner.
key_facts: Keep at least two owners with their own accounts
Admin, Editor or Guest is not a backup owner
answer:
1. We recommend keeping at least two people in your organization as team owners, each using their own Plausible account [1].
2. For an existing team, an owner can invite someone or change an existing member's role in Team Settings → General [1].
3. Make sure any new owner accepts their invitation before you rely on their access [1].
4. Set up another Owner before planned leave or a departure, or after recovering access [1].

evidence.title: Recover access when an owner is unavailable
evidence.text:
We recommend keeping at least two people in your organization as team owners, each using their own Plausible account. This lets another owner continue managing the team, sites and subscription when one person is unavailable.

If your sites are under **My personal sites**, create a team and add another owner. For an existing team, an owner can invite someone or change an existing member's role in **Team Settings → General**. Make sure any new owner accepts their invitation before you rely on their access.

An Admin, Editor or Guest is not a backup owner. Set up another **Owner** before planned leave or a departure, or after recovering access.
